messages.subject: how to build a GUI with shiny library
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering to build a complex Graphical User Interface under R with the shiny library.
I already made the shiny tutorials on the rstudio website, but I don't understand how to set up the project with the shiny files (UI and server).

I should need to use multiple UI files and multiple SERVER files, in order to have a modular code and to easily release it as an R package.

Someone has some suggestions? tutorials for multiple interfaces in shiny? 

Thanks in advance,
Inzirio

messages.author: d48c25039d976859
messages.subject: Re: how to build a GUI with shiny library
parts:
Here is a barebones dashboard code that you can copy in paste into your R console and run. I am assuming you have the Shiny library and dashboard library installed.


################Bare Bones Shiny Dashboard

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title = "Basic dashboard"),
  dashboardSidebar(),
  dashboardBody(

###################Add Dashboard UI Stuff Here
    # Boxes need to be put in a row (or column)
    fluidRow(
      box(plotOutput("plot1", height = 250)),

      box(
        title = "Controls",
        sliderInput("slider", "Number of observations:", 1, 100, 50)
      )
    )

####################End Dashdoard Body UI Stuff Here
 

  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

####################Start Server Calculations Here
  set.seed(122)
  histdata <- rnorm(500)

  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    data <- histdata[seq_len(input$slider)]
    hist(data)
  })
####################End Server Calculations Here

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

 

The tone of your post almost makes me feel like you are expecting build a complicated and atractive dashboard in a matter of minutes.

You can make aswesome dashboards with Shiny, but it will take some time if you are new at it. On the other hand, one of the best things about Shiny is that you can do some some pretty monumental things with only a few lines of code.

messages.subject: Re: how to build a GUI with shiny library
parts:
People tend to do this with a single app that contains different navbarPage tabs: https://vnijs.shinyapps.io/marketing

The thing to keep in mind about defining shiny UI, is that the main tool for managing complexity is the same tool as everywhere else in R: the function. Since Shiny user interfaces are defined using function calls, take advantage of that fact by reusing and encapsulating UI creation logic into functions. The same can be said for defining server logic--write functions, and when those functions get too complicated, split them into more functions.

If you want multiple apps, then you can write totally distinct apps that happen to be hosted on the same instance of Shiny Server. Passing data between them is not as well-defined, but you can come up with your own schemes using query string parameters and server side persistence.

I'm embedding shiny apps in my dashboard like this:

##server file

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)



shinyServer(function(input,output,session) {
  
  output$ui <- renderUI({
    eval(parse(system.file("examples/01_hello/ui.R", package="shiny")))
  })
  subserver <- eval(parse(system.file("examples/01_hello/server.R", package="shiny")))
  subserver(input,output)
  
})


##ui.R
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

shinyUI(dashboardPage(
  ## HEADER
  dashboardHeader(title="",
                  titleWidth = 335),
  
  dashboardSidebar(
    width = 335
  ),
  dashboardBody(
    htmlOutput('ui')
  )
    
))


you can create inputs which change the location of the app ui and server locations this way and handle everything in the server controller
